entries.reason: Reached only through firebase-tools' Pub/Sub emulator support. firebase-tools 15.30.2 is the current latest (raised from 15.29.0 on 2026-09-21) and still resolves @google-cloud/pubsub 5.x, which pins @opentelemetry/core 1.x; npm's only proposed remedy is firebase-tools@10.1.1, a five-major CLI downgrade. The `firebase-tools` package name is listed here because npm flags the CLI itself as a vulnerable node whenever any of its transitive advisories are open; the CLI is a devDependency and is never shipped.
entries.reachability: Not reachable in any deployed artifact. The advisory is unbounded memory allocation in W3C Baggage propagation, which requires processing attacker-controlled baggage headers. This copy exists only inside firebase-tools, a devDependency; GoalPlace ships no OpenTelemetry instrumentation and no deployed service parses baggage headers through this package. `npm audit --omit=dev` reports zero production advisories as of 2026-09-21.
entries.mitigation: Not shipped. Runs only on developer and CI machines invoking the Firebase CLI, against local emulators rather than untrusted network input.

entries.reason: firebase-tools 15.30.2 (current latest) declares csv-parse ^5.0.4, so the patched 7.0.2 cannot be resolved without an upstream bump; npm's only proposed remedy is firebase-tools@10.1.1, a five-major CLI downgrade. Nothing in this repository depends on csv-parse directly.
entries.reachability: Not reachable. The advisory is prototype replacement through the `columns` option when a CSV header names `__proto__`. Verified in node_modules on 2026-09-21: the single consumer is `firebase-tools/lib/commands/auth-import.js:50`, which calls `parse()` with no options at all, so the `columns` code path is never entered and records are returned as plain arrays. That command (`firebase auth:import`) reads a file the developer names on the command line; it is never invoked by any deployed artifact and no network input reaches it. `npm audit --omit=dev` reports zero production advisories.
entries.mitigation: Not shipped. The vulnerable option is never used, and the only caller is a developer-run CLI command over a local file. Clears when firebase-tools advances to csv-parse >= 7.0.2.

entries.reason: firebase-tools 15.30.2 (current latest) declares stream-json ^1.7.3; the patched release is on the 3.x line and cannot be resolved without an upstream bump. npm reports a fix as available but `npm audit fix` declines it because it would violate the CLI's declared range. Nothing in this repository depends on stream-json directly.
entries.reachability: Not reachable from untrusted input. The advisory is quadratic-time behaviour in the Pick/Ignore/Filter/Replace filters on deeply nested JSON, a denial of service against the process running the parser. Verified in node_modules on 2026-09-21: the three consumers are `firebase-tools/lib/commands/auth-import.js:84` (Pick over a JSON file the developer names on the command line), `firebase-tools/lib/database/import.js:137` (Filter over a JSON file the developer names for `database:import`), and `firebase-tools/lib/frameworks/next/index.js:407` (Pick over the stdout of `npm ls --omit=dev --json` run in the developer's own source directory). Every input is chosen by the developer on their own machine; the worst outcome is a stalled CLI process. No deployed artifact contains this package and `npm audit --omit=dev` reports zero production advisories.
entries.mitigation: Not shipped. Runs only on developer and CI machines, only over files and command output the developer controls. Clears when firebase-tools advances to stream-json >= 3.4.1.
